article.title: [Dell][Wistron][GhostRider] Camera noise when AC plug-in/plug-out with dGPU config
article.description:
Camera noise when AC plug in with dGPU config



Open Camera APP
Plug-in or Plug-out AC
Camera preview shows garbage or lag


System scope available from customer = no (reason : Unable to collect Intel® SST log)
article.subject: bug
article.bugfixdescription: add 100ms sleep after L23D () in \"ON\" ASL code to follow PCIe spec claims SW needs to delay 100ms after link training complete

IDST 27.2
DOEs in progress.Upstream tracing confirms MSI interrupts are reaching the core without delay, ruling out issues in the front-end path. Remaining gaps include validating VTU MSI acknowledgment behavior and checking for possible software-side interrupt handling delays.
Next steps are to capture downstream traces to confirm VTU ACK timing and involve the MTC team to analyze SW interrupt servicing latency.

Update WW23.3 status 1. the miss service error was caused by the isoch frame id late. assign xfervalidadvdq   = xferadvdq && (latchdcntxnoresppending || !xferblockenreg);     end else if ((currentxferst==WAIT4RESP) && xferresphmdone && isofrmidlate && (schreqctrlpst == 2'b10) && cfgcfcen)  begin       xferadvdq         <= #TP 1'b1; 2. There is no devdbrang for ~108ms before the xfervalidadvdq asserted, it's aligned to the xHCI driver log, the URB completion return after ~100ms. 3. The last devdbrang TRB was completed, we could observe the MSI fire after ~15ms. However, the driver do not process the MSI (eventhandlerbusyd0i2 = 0x1). Current suspecting is MSI may have been delayed. Similar issue in LNL: https://hsdes.intel.com/appstore/article-one/#/article/16023550352 In LNL, the VTd drop the MSI. 4. The issue cannot be observed after disabling VTd. However, the issue still cannot repro after re-enabling VTd. Next step 1. ask the customer to disable VTd and repro 2. check how to recover the issue repro 3. check who block the MSI (posted MWr -> PSF6 -> PSF0 -> IOC)
